memories.memory_text: I reached through the letterbox, felt the cold metal of the key, and pulled it out to open the door—my own house, but it didn’t feel like coming home.

I moved around Kendall Davenport’s coffin with the razor in hand, the cord stretched tight from the lamp above him—my reflection flickered in the blade as I shaved, the hum of the motor the only sound in the room.
I was watching Kendall Davenport’s coffin ahead when Noel Everett said he couldn’t believe it—he was surprised Kendall Davenport didn’t show up for work. Said he was always on time.
Linden Sawyer muttered it was a bloody funny thing—Kendall Davenport was calm, like gentle Jesus, for six years, then suddenly did something like this. I just said, yeah, a bloody funny thing.
I asked Noel Everett, 'Since when did he drink whisky?' and saw the doubt flicker across his face—nobody had an answer, nobody even knew.
I leaned in and told Noel Everett to let me know if anyone asked for me—set myself up as someone looking, someone watching. Then I asked about Terry Prescott, knowing he might be the first real lead.
I walked past Alex Whitaker and blew him a kiss just as he was trying to sound tough—I could see the surprise on his face, and Casey Warren didn’t stop me, so I knew I’d already taken the room.

When Casey Warren offered condolences about Kendall Davenport, I just said 'Yep'—short, no emotion, because showing anything would’ve been weakness, and he needed to see I wasn’t here to grieve, I was here to push.

I stood by that crushed Hillman in the scrapyard and asked Billy Laws if the steering was faulty—then the brakes. He said both were fine. When he told me Kendall Davenport was drunk, I just said, 'Was he?' like I didn’t believe it, or didn’t want to.

I picked up the wooden casket from the Stonebridge Warehouse table, felt its weight—lighter than I expected—and put it on the side table without opening it. When Shawn Finch asked if Kendall Davenport was staying the night, I just said, 'Funny.'
I looked at Shawn Finch and told her I fancied her, that I wanted to touch her, to make love to her—then asked her softly, 'Where are you?'
I asked Harper Dalton if she was wearing the sexy, silk ones, then told her to take her bra off—she hesitated, but I told her again, softly, to go on.
I told him to move slowly, to imagine it was me doing it—my voice, my presence, like I was there in his skin.
I took the ticket Jordan Hollis handed me, smiled, and asked who to thank—knowing full well it wasn’t a favor, but a threat.
I tore the ticket in half and threw it in the gutter—then yanked the the brass box door open and slammed it into the man getting out, shattering the window and spraying blood.

I pulled the chain in the stall while Jordan Hollis was sitting there, watching the door like a cornered animal—he bolted upright, scared out of his wits before I even spoke. Then I told him, 'Time's up, Jordan Hollis,' and smiled; he knew the game was over.
I picked up Kendall Davenport's casket on the stairs.
I opened the door, pushed Jordan Hollis inside, and shut Shawn Finch out. When she threatened the police, I told her no, you won't—and I knew she wouldn't.
I had Jordan Hollis doubled over in pain, screaming—he finally spat out 'Taylor North' after I squeezed hard. I knew he could talk if he wanted to.
After Jordan Hollis gasped out 'Burnham,' I connected Taylor North to the arcades along the coast—Noel Everett even confirmed he'd been to Westsea. The pieces were falling into place.
I saw Taylor North get out of his white Bentley and kick a young man into the lily pond after yelling about someone spewing on his goldfish.

I parked and watched from behind a tree. I saw Taylor North arrive and storm into Silverbrook Theater. He shouted at Sandra, then passed an upstairs window while she locked herself in a bedroom. I heard him yell, 'Unlock the door, you bitch.' I opened the front door and went in.
I said I made a mistake—twice—because Jordan Hollis lied; Taylor North didn't recognize me or the Fletchers, and that laugh came out before I could stop it, cold and sharp in the quiet room.
I was with Shawn Finch, the bedsprings moving gently, and then her laughter—just before the door opened and their legs appeared, blocking the light.
I covered Drew Rivers with the the brass badge, took his the brass badge, and made him open the coalshed door before bolting him inside—then got in the the brass box and left.

I didn't believe her when she said Kendall Davenport threatened to kill himself after she turned him down. Kendall Davenport wasn't like that—he was too careful, too controlled. I snapped her sunglasses in half just to shut out the lie, but it still rang in my head.

I grabbed her arm and shouted in her face—she had to know I wasn't leaving until I found out who killed Kendall Davenport. Then I saw Rowan Keller's Jaguar coming, and when Drew Rivers called my name, I knew she'd ratted me out. I hit her and jumped the rail before they could reach me.
I remember asking Blair Hawthorne how she found me, and then her slamming the the brass box to a stop, saying the demon king had sent her with a spell—some twisted certainty that I’d show up.
Taylor North offered me five thousand dollars and the name Casey Warren, saying he was responsible for Kendall Davenport's death—but I didn't believe him. That wasn't enough to make me act.
I asked Blair Hawthorne who set her up in the apartment, and she said Taylor North—simple as that. Then she told me Casey Warren doesn’t suspect a thing because he thinks she’s simple.

I turned on the projector after she left the room and saw the brass lantern—'The Teacher's Pet'—with Blair Hawthorne bare-breasted in front of a blackboard, then Reese Dalton offering a schoolgirl a ride in a the brass box. I didn’t see the girl’s face, but it was clear what kind of operation this was.
I stood over Blair Hawthorne in the bath and asked about the girl in the brass lantern, and when she kept lying, I grabbed her and held her under the water until she coughed up the name—Drew Arden.

When she said the girl was Drew Arden, I told her the name Evan Vaughn wasn't just mine—it was hers too, her father was my brother Kendall Davenport, and he was murdered, and I made her get out of the bath.
I raised the the brass badge to throw it clear into the sea—just let it go—and then something hit me hard, like a punch from nowhere, and I fell.

dialogue_exemplars: Drink up, Parker Sinclair. Drink up. I want you to drink all of that. Do you understand? Drink up. Just like it was with my brother, Kendall Davenport. Go on, son. Drink up.
You bloody whore. Kendall Davenport was too careful to die like that. Who killed him?
Oh, really. You're getting very optimistic in your old age, aren't you, Jordan Hollis?
Hold it! Hold it! (looking her in the eye) Who killed Kendall Davenport, Reese Dalton?

I banged on Sandra's door, shouting for her to unlock it—she thinks she can shut me out, but this is still my house and she's not locking me out like some stranger.

I confronted that bastard in my sitting room, demanding to know who sent him at two in the morning, and when he just stood there laughing, I swung at him—next thing I knew, my head was ringing and I was collapsing into the chair, hurt and humiliated.
I wasn't even there when they brought up my name—just some joke between Evan Vaughn and Shawn Finch, like I’m something to laugh about.

I offered Evan Vaughn five grand and the name Casey Warren, trying to make it clear we had the same enemy, but he walked out, shouting it wasn't good enough—like I was just another liar trying to use him.
I set her up in that apartment, and I made sure there was a projector—she knows what it’s for, especially when she’s the one on screen.
I saw the brass lantern and I wanted to meet Drew Arden — that’s what I told Terry Prescott when I paid him a visit.
I told them I didn't want any cooking in the restaurant—just put a hatch in the wall. Then that bloody the brass box screeched up, and I had to go see who the madman was.
I came out to the top tier.

I was coming down the stairs when Evan Vaughn suddenly appeared and punched me hard in the gut—knocked the wind out of me. I barely got out that I had to show the brass lantern to Kendall Davenport, that it was the only way to get at them.
I lined up the shot through the scope, saw Evan Vaughn by the water, raised the rifle, and pulled the trigger—just a quiet whoosh, then he went down.

memories.memory_text: I swung around when Evan Vaughn said my name—didn't see him coming, heart just dropped. Grey suit, cap, glasses—I thought I was hidden.
He took my sunglasses off, looked right into my eyes—called them piss holes in the snow. Felt exposed, like he saw through everything.
I'm gripping the wheel, tired as hell but pushing through—champagne corks popping behind me, voices buzzing, the radio spitting out race results while I keep the Cadillac steady down the road.
I jumped up when Alex Whitaker said Evan Vaughn was here—then Casey Warren dropped it, said I worked for him, like it was some kind of joke. Evan Vaughn looked at me like he saw through everything.
I told Evan Vaughn straight—Casey Warren didn't like what he was doing, and Terry Marlowe and Finley Rivers wouldn't like it either. Then I made Alex Whitaker follow after him.
They named me. Evan Vaughn asked if I set it up, and Blair Hawthorne said yeah. Now he thinks I pulled her.
I hear the girl's voice on the phone—'Parker Sinclair, he's come for Terry Prescott'—and I know it's about me, even though I don't see her. The call tightens my chest, makes me move faster.
I brought Drew Arden in, used my connection through Reese Dalton. Didn't think it'd go this far.
I stepped off the Land Rover, legs unsteady on the gangplank—the jetty swayed underfoot, water slapping below. The ferry was already chugging in, engine loud, no time to stop.

I laughed and told Evan Vaughn he was finished. I said I'd bloody finished him. I told Drew Rivers to tell Evan Vaughn I'd told Finley Rivers about him and Harper Dalton. I asked if Finley Rivers believed us at first, then said Rowan Keller talked to him.
I laughed and told Evan Vaughn his the brass box needed a wash — then gave the signal. The Land Rover hit the Sunbeam twice, and it went into the river.
I told Casey Warren Finley Rivers wanted to speak to him—had to shout over the music just to be heard. Phone was hot in my hand, whole place buzzing like a damn hive.
Casey Warren looked at me while talking to Evan Vaughn, said something about it being arranged—like I’m part of some deal now. I kept pouring my drink, hands shaky, didn’t trust that look.
Casey Warren called me out—just my name, calm like it was nothing, but it wasn't nothing. I was moving, always moving, but his voice made me stop.
I stepped out into the cold dawn air, the noise of The Midnight Visit still pounding behind me, and got into the Cadillac fast—just drove.
I bolted down the stairs and sprinted for the road, lungs burning, knowing he was up there somewhere—always above me, footsteps echoing just out of reach.
I saw the the brass box—maybe a way out—then froze when I saw the the brass badge raised above me; his voice cut through the dawn, and I ducked under the jetty instead.
I'm running across the Cedar Grove Hospital, pebbles crunching under my feet, lungs burning with every breath. I can see the factory smoke in the distance, and then—Evan Vaughn’s there, watching me.
I tripped and went down hard on the Cedar Grove Hospital—sand in my mouth, heart slamming—Evan Vaughn right behind me. Got up fast, didn’t look back, just ran around the headland.
I'm sinking in the black mud, each step dragging like my legs are made of lead, and I can see Evan Vaughn gaining on me out of the corner of my eye.

I took the cap off the bottle, hands shaking, and poured the whisky into my mouth—couldn't stop it from spilling, burning down my face, suit soaked, Evan Vaughn yelling in my ear about Kendall Davenport, about the laugh, about the the brass box.
I was choking, couldn't breathe, legs gave way—then the the brass badge came down, hard, blacked out fast, didn't even see it coming.
I'm falling—cold, weightless—then the water hits hard, black dust choking the light as the waves close over me.
